title: Postgres serverless protocol conformance corpus
description: One corpus document: fixtures that put a real PostgreSQL into a known state, and cases that each describe one complete HTTP exchange against a server in that state. See CONFORMANCE.md for why cases are shaped this way, in particular why expected values carry JSON text rather than parsed values.

spec_version.description: The SPEC.md version these cases check, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. It moves with the spec, not with any implementation.

version.description: Corpus version. Cases may be added within a version; an existing case's expectation changes only with a version bump, so a report against v1 stays meaningful.

sql.description: Idempotent SQL creating and populating the fixture's tables. Runs against a scratch database that several runs may share, so it must tolerate already existing.

id.description: group/name. Stable, so a report can cite it.

level.description: Conformance level this case belongs to. See SPEC.md section 10.

spec.description: The SPEC.md section this case pins, for example "6.1". A failure should point at a rule, not at a test name.

note.description: Present when the case is not self-evident. Read these.

fixture.description: Name of the fixture this case needs. Omitted when the case needs no tables.

requires.description: A condition the harness must arrange that is configuration rather than data. A harness that cannot arrange it MUST report the case skipped, never passed.

compare.description: exact compares the serialized JSON. parses_equal is for the spellings SPEC.md Appendix B leaves unsettled: the harness parses both sides as JSON and also accepts the alternative spellings a value lists in `also`. A report counts these separately.

headers.description: Symbolic, not literal. The harness decides whether to send the vendor-prefixed or unprefixed spelling, which is how the same corpus tests both and their precedence without duplicating cases.

spelling.description: Which header spelling to send. "both" sends conflicting values to test that the unprefixed one wins.

omit_connection_string.description: Send no connection string at all, to test admission's handling of a missing one.

body.description: The request body, sent verbatim as JSON. A string here is sent as a raw body, which is how malformed-JSON cases are expressed.

status.description: Required HTTP status. For error cases whose status is a documented server choice (SPEC.md 7.2), use status_class instead.

status_class.description: Accept any 4xx or 5xx. Used where SPEC.md 7.2 leaves the mapping to the implementation but still requires the error shape.

fields.description: Checked field by field, in order. Only the members listed are compared, since tableID and columnID vary by database.

rows.description: Row by row. An object-mode row is an object keyed by column name; an array-mode row is an array. Each value is a json-wrapper (see json_value) so the encoding is pinned, which is the whole point: "9007199254740993" and 9007199254740993 are different answers.

results.description: For a batch: one entry per statement, each shaped like a single-statement expect.

error.description: For an error response. Only the members present are compared. Field names are the client's, per SPEC.md 7.1.

has_fields.description: Members that must be present and non-null. This is what catches a server emitting schemaName where the client reads schema.

must_not_contain.description: Substrings that must not appear anywhere in the response, used to check that a connection string is not leaked in an error.

json_value.description: A value whose JSON encoding is pinned. `json` holds the exact JSON text the server must produce for this value. Comparing serialized text rather than parsed values is deliberate: most languages cannot tell a JSON string from a JSON number after parsing, and that distinction is the single most important rule in the spec.

also.description: Other JSON texts a server may emit for this value. Honoured only when the case's compare is parses_equal, and only for spellings SPEC.md Appendix B leaves unsettled.
